newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rally on U.S., peso bonds surge.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rally on U.S., peso bonds surge.

text.p: Argentine bonds rallied Tuesday to finish a session with buying across the board, spurred by modest U.S. consumer price figures.
"As the U.S. figures were good, it gave an impulse to bonds here, above all the (peso-denominated) "Pro 1" and "Pre 3"," said a trader at a foreign bank.
The Bocon Proveedor 1 due 2007 surged 2.30 pesos to 99.00.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 7/8 to 88-1/2, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.70 to 125.05.
U.S. December consumer prices rose 0.3 percent, in line with analyst expectations, while the core rate advanced 0.1 percent, below the 0.2 percent increase forecast by analysts.

"U.S. rates are now expected to remain stable," said another trader. After strong U.S. indicators last week, worries re-emerged that the Federal Reserve would raise rates in February but those fears subsided with Tuesday's data.

Traders said both foreign and domestic investors also ventured further out on the Argentine dollar curve, buying such bonds as the dollar Bocon Proveedor 2 due 2007. That paper rose $1.55, or 1.4 percent to 112.50.
"Investors are looking for bonds with higher yield," said the first trader.

The placement Tuesday of 250 million pesos in 91-day treasury bills at a discount rate of 6.40 percent and 250 million pesos of 182-day bills at a rate of 6.90 percent also helped the market's mood, said traders.
Players said they hoped the sharp pickup in trading volumes this session would be sustained in coming days helping to maintain prices at their higher levels.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 5.38 percent from 5.53 percent.
